1	---
2	name: meeting-sync
3	description: >-
4	  Sync new Fireflies transcripts into the SecondBrain vault; audit vault filenames for
5	  drift against Fireflies titles. Idempotent. Use when the user says "sync meetings",
6	  "pull latest meetings", "/meeting-sync", "update meeting notes", "any new meetings?",
7	  or when invoked by weekly-review. Also for filename drift — "are any meeting files
8	  misnamed?", "did a meeting get renamed after export?", "why is this meeting titled
9	  differently in Fireflies than in the vault?", "audit the meeting filenames". Do not
10	  use to rename generic titles inside Fireflies (use name-meetings) or to search what
11	  was said in transcripts (use pp-fireflies).
12	argument-hint: "[days-back]"
13	---
14	
15	# Meeting Sync
16	
17	Pull new Fireflies transcripts into the SecondBrain vault. Each meeting becomes one markdown file at `Inbox/meetings/YYYY-MM-DD_<title>.md`.
18	
19	## Paths — shared config
20	
21	Vault and state-file paths live in `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.<platform>.json` (single source of truth):
22	- `vault_inbox_meetings` — platform-specific export target
23	- `meeting_sync_state_file` — idempotency ledger (`.sync-state.json` in that folder)
24	- `meeting_lookback_days` — default window (14)
25	
26	`scripts/sync.py` reads these itself; don't hardcode paths elsewhere. If the vault ever moves, edit the config only.
27	
28	sync.py passes `--limit 100000` to `transcripts find` — the CLI's default is 100, which silently truncates large backfills. Don't remove that flag.
29	
30	## Prerequisite — one-time auth
31	
32	Auth is the `FIREFLIES_API_KEY` environment variable (see the `pp-fireflies` skill's Auth Setup). Verify with `fireflies-pp-cli doctor --agent` — the JSON must show `"auth": "configured"`. `scripts/sync.py` runs this check itself and exits with code 4 if auth is missing. In that case, stop and tell the user:
33	
34	> Fireflies isn't authenticated yet. On the Mac, store the key in the Keychain with `security add-generic-password -U -s FIREFLIES_API_KEY -a "$USER" -w` (it prompts for the key; `~/.zshrc` exports it); on Windows, set it under System Properties → Environment Variables. Then open a new terminal. After that, `/meeting-sync` will work.
35	
36	Do not try to fix auth yourself (no `auth set-token` — the env var is the canonical mechanism). Then exit.
37	
38	## Sync flow
39	
40	### 1. Run the pipeline script
41	
42	The deterministic pipeline (doctor check → CLI sync → find → state diff → export → state update) is fully implemented in `scripts/sync.py`. Two-phase invocation:
43	
44	**Phase A — list pending, check titles:**
45	```bash
46	python scripts/sync.py --list-only [--days-back N]
47	```
48	Prints a JSON array of not-yet-exported transcripts: `[{"id", "title", "date"}]`. Diagnostics go to stderr.
49	
50	**Phase B — export:**
51	```bash
52	python scripts/sync.py --no-sync [--days-back N]
53	```
54	Prints a JSON array of newly exported absolute file paths (`--no-sync` skips the redundant DB refresh Phase A just did). Exports are detected by diffing the vault directory listing before/after each export — never "most recent .md" — so a no-op export can't claim an unrelated file.
55	
56	`[days-back]` argument from the user maps to `--days-back N`; otherwise the config default applies.
57	
58	### 2. Between phases: generic-title judgment (model's job)
59	
60	The user does not name their Fireflies meetings consistently. Generic titles produce useless filenames in the vault. Check each pending `title` from Phase A against the generic patterns documented in the `name-meetings` skill (empty, `Zoom Meeting`, `Recording`, `Meeting`, date-only, etc.).
61	
62	- **0 generics:** run Phase B immediately, silently.
63	- **1–3 generics:** use `AskUserQuestion` once — question: "N of the new meetings have generic titles. Name them before exporting?" with options **[Propose names first / Export as-is]**. If "Propose names first", invoke the `name-meetings` skill scoped to just these IDs, then re-run Phase A to pick up renamed titles before Phase B.
64	- **4+ generics:** report the count and suggest: *"Several new meetings have generic titles. Run `/name-meetings` to clean them up — I'll proceed with the export either way."* Then run Phase B without blocking.
65	
66	This keeps the rename loop tight at sync-time without blocking the pipeline.
67	
68	### 3. Augment each exported file (model's job)
69	
70	For each path in Phase B's JSON output, the file is raw Fireflies markdown. Insert the fixed 5-section header from `assets/meeting-header.md` (this skill's folder) at the top — after frontmatter, before any existing content. Read the asset and prepend it verbatim.
71	
72	Leave the Fireflies-generated transcript and summary below this block intact. This gives the user **5 fixed sections to fill in or curate** during interview-me / weekly-review, on top of the raw Fireflies content.
73	
74	### 4. Tag each exported file with its project (script's job)
75	
76	After the header is in place, pass the same paths to the tagger:
77	
78	```bash
79	python scripts/tag_project.py <path> [<path> ...]
80	```
81	
82	It asks TypeSafe's Jev which `portfolio.json` project each meeting is mainly about, and adds `- project/<PortfolioName>` under `## Project tags` only when the answer is confident. It always adds one `<!-- jev-project: ... -->` line recording what was asked and answered, which is also how a rerun knows to skip the note. `meeting-prep` reads the `- project/` line to find a project's meetings.
83	
84	It never blocks the sync: no key, no network or no transcript just leaves the note untagged and logs to stderr. Relay any `WARNING` lines. Run it only after step 3, because notes without a `## Project tags` header are skipped.
85	
86	## Drift audit (periodic, not every sync)
87	
88	A vault filename is a snapshot of the Fireflies title at export time. Titles get renamed afterwards, so the two drift apart. `scripts/audit_filenames.py` detects this by asking the export CLI to regenerate every filename into a scratch dir and diffing against the ledger — **the slug algorithm is never reimplemented**, the CLI is the authority.
89	
90	```bash
91	python scripts/audit_filenames.py [--since YYYY-MM-DD] [--skip-linkcheck] [--report PATH]
92	```
93	
94	Run it from `weekly-review`, or on demand — **not** on every sync (it spawns one CLI call per ledger entry, ~2-4 min for a full vault). Same exit codes as sync.py; drift itself is not an error, read the counts in the JSON.
95	
96	It classifies every mismatch, and the classes need different responses:
97	
98	- **`regression`** — the vault name is good and Fireflies has reverted to an auto-generated stamp (`Jan_19_0445_PM`, `Untitled`, `Audio_Message`). **Never re-export these — it destroys the good name.** Fix the title upstream in Fireflies instead. Note the API refuses title updates on some older meetings; if so, say so and leave the vault alone (the ledger already protects it).
99	- **`semantic`** — the title genuinely differs in meaning. Usually two generations of AI naming rather than rot, so it needs a human call, not an automatic rename. Surface it, don't act.
100	- **`cosmetic`** — same words, different separators (`RTP_UpperExtremity` vs `RTP___Upper_Extremity`). Ignore; re-exporting is pure churn.
101	
102	Before proposing any rename, check `inbound_links` in the output. Renaming a vault file breaks `[[wikilinks]]` from weekly-review notes and `GRAPH_REPORT.md`. Rewrite those links in the same pass or leave the file alone.
103	
104	## Output to user
105	
106	When done, report:
107	- N transcripts found in the window (stderr line from sync.py)
108	- M new exports written, K tagged with a project
109	- Path: `Inbox/meetings/`
110	- If 0 new: just say "No new meetings since last sync."
111	
112	Keep it to 3 lines.
113	
114	## Error handling
115	
116	sync.py exit codes: 0 ok, 2 usage/config, 3 sync/find failure, 4 auth not configured.
117	
118	- **Exit 4 (auth):** deliver the auth message from Prerequisite above, stop.
119	- **Exit 3 (sync/find):** report the stderr error verbatim, do not try to recover. The user may need to refresh their API key.
120	- **Export fails for one transcript:** sync.py logs a warning to stderr and continues with the rest; relay which one failed.
121	- **State file corrupted:** sync.py backs it up to `.sync-state.json.bak` and recreates fresh automatically (re-export is idempotent on the filesystem because filenames are deterministic per CLI); flag this in the report if the warning appears.
122	
123	## Gotchas
124	
125	- **Two tag vocabularies share `## Project tags`.** Hand tags are topic words (`project/rtp`, `project/load-monitoring`). Jev tags are exact `portfolio.json` names (`project/Sport_Tech_Vetting`). The tagger only appends and never edits or removes a hand tag.
126	- **Measured before shipping, so don't tune the question here.** The question wording and the 0.60 threshold in `tag_project.py` were tested blind on 40 meetings (TypeSafe_Sandbox `docs/FIREFLIES_PROJECT_TAG.md`, 2026-09-22). Jev was confident on 36, and right on 33 of those. It never confidently tagged a non-project meeting, but it found only 7 of 11 real project meetings. OKRs_2026-27 was the repeat miss. Judge any wording change against meetings the test didn't use.
127	- **A missing tag is not evidence the meeting is unrelated.** The marker line says `none of these` or `(unsure)`. Callers still fall back to text search.
128	- **Probabilities wobble by a few points between runs** (for example 0.83 vs 0.81 on the same note). Notes near 0.60 can go either way, which is one reason the marker is written once and not re-asked.
129	- **Vault notes can mix CRLF and LF lines.** The tagger splices in its lines and never re-encodes the file. Don't "clean up" line endings in this script: an earlier draft did, and rewrote about 50 lines of one note.
130	
131	## What NOT to do
132	
133	- **Don't re-implement steps the script owns** — doctor, CLI sync, find, state diff, export, state update all live in `scripts/sync.py`.
134	- **Don't identify exports by "newest .md file"** — that's the exact bug the directory-diff in sync.py fixes.
135	- **Don't detect filename drift by pattern-matching for "generic-looking" names** — that both misses real drift and invents fake drift. Use `audit_filenames.py`, which compares against what the export CLI actually produces.
136	- **Don't bulk re-export to "clean up" filenames.** Most mismatches are cosmetic or a second valid naming generation, and the `regression` class gets actively worse. Re-export only what a human approved.
137	- **Don't modify the Fireflies-generated content** of the exported file — only PREPEND the header from `assets/meeting-header.md`. The transcript and AI summary stay untouched.
138	- **Don't sync every interaction.** Run sync only when explicitly invoked OR when called by weekly-review / fireflies-intake.
139

1	---
2	name: fireflies-intake
3	description: >-
4	  One-command Fireflies pipeline — sync new meeting transcripts into the SecondBrain

---
name: fireflies-intake
description: >-
  One-command Fireflies pipeline — sync new meeting transcripts into the SecondBrain
  vault, rename generically-titled meetings, then report exactly what was ingested. Use
  when the user says "/fireflies-intake", "ingest my recent fireflies meetings", "sync
  meetings that aren't in the second brain yet", "pull in the new meetings", "meeting
  ingestion", or asks whether all recent meetings have been ingested. Do not use to
  search what was said in transcripts (use pp-fireflies).
argument-hint: "[since-date]"
---

# Fireflies Intake

Replaces the recurring hand-typed sequence: "ingest my recent fireflies meetings" → "some have generic names, rename them" → "is everything from <date> in the second brain?" Runs the full chain in order, unattended, then reports.

This is an orchestrator — the actual work lives in existing skills. Invoke them, don't reimplement them.

## Step 1 — Rename first

Invoke the **name-meetings** skill in its **Unattended mode** (declare it explicitly when invoking) to find meetings with generic titles (empty, "Zoom Meeting", "Recording", date-only) and apply structured names. Renaming BEFORE sync means the vault notes are created under their proper names — no cleanup pass later.

- Unattended mode applies only HIGH-confidence renames without approval; anything with weak evidence (vague gist, missing summary) is written to the `review[]` array of the pending-renames file (`pending_renames_file` in `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.<platform>.json`) for later interactive review — never guessed and applied.

## Step 2 — Sync

Invoke the **meeting-sync** skill to pull all transcripts not yet in the SecondBrain vault. It is idempotent — run it over the full recent window rather than trying to compute the delta yourself.

## Step 3 — Verify completeness

Compare the Fireflies meeting list for the sync window against the vault's meeting notes (the pp-fireflies CLI's local database is the cheapest source for the meeting list; the vault folder is `vault_inbox_meetings` and the export ledger is `meeting_sync_state_file`, both in `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.<platform>.json`). Every meeting must be accounted for: ingested now, ingested previously, or intentionally skipped (with the reason).

## Step 4 — Report

```
## Fireflies Intake — <date>

**Renamed:** <n> meetings (<old → new>, one line each; or "none needed")
**Ingested:** <n> new meetings → <vault folder path>
   - <meeting name> (<date>)
**Already in vault:** <n>
**Skipped/failed:** <list with reasons, or "none">
**Queued for review:** <n> low-confidence rename proposals in .pending-renames.json (omit line if 0)
```

If the user also wants the new notes graphed into the knowledge graph, they'll say so — offer `/graphify` as a one-line follow-up only when new meetings were actually ingested.

## Rules

- Never duplicate a vault note; trust meeting-sync's idempotency and say "already in vault" rather than re-ingesting.
- If the Fireflies API or CLI auth fails, report which step failed and stop — don't half-ingest silently.
- An empty run is a valid result: "No new meetings since <date>" is the complete report.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""meeting-sync deterministic pipeline (steps 1-5 of SKILL.md).

Pipeline: doctor auth check -> fireflies-pp-cli sync -> transcripts find
-> state-file diff -> export loop (directory-diff file detection)
-> state-file update.

stdout: a JSON array. Full run: absolute paths of newly exported .md files.
--list-only: pending (not-yet-exported) transcripts as
{"id", "title", "date"} objects, no export performed.
All diagnostics go to stderr.

Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 unexpected, 2 usage/config, 3 sync/find failure,
4 auth not configured.

Paths come from the platform-specific shared config at ../../_shared/.
(vault_inbox_meetings, meeting_sync_state_file, meeting_lookback_days).
"""

import argparse
import json
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

CONFIG_PATH = (
    Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
    / "_shared"
    / ("config.windows.json" if sys.platform == "win32" else "config.macos.json")
)


def log(msg: str) -> None:
    print(msg, file=sys.stderr, flush=True)


def die(code: int, msg: str) -> "None":
    log(f"ERROR: {msg}")
    sys.exit(code)


def load_config() -> dict:
    try:
        with open(CONFIG_PATH, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            cfg = json.load(f)
    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as e:
        die(2, f"cannot read shared config {CONFIG_PATH}: {e}")
    for key in ("vault_root", "vault_inbox_meetings", "meeting_sync_state_file"):
        if key not in cfg:
            die(2, f"shared config missing required key: {key}")
    return cfg


def resolve_cli(cfg: dict) -> str:
    configured = cfg.get("fireflies_cli")
    if configured and Path(configured).is_file():
        return str(configured)
    exe = shutil.which("fireflies-pp-cli")
    if not exe:
        die(2, "fireflies-pp-cli not found on PATH")
    return exe


def run_cli(exe: str, args: list, timeout: int = 300) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
    return subprocess.run(
        [exe] + args, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout
    )


def check_auth(exe: str) -> None:
    """Step 1: doctor. Requires JSON field "auth": "configured"
    (key comes from the FIREFLIES_API_KEY environment variable)."""
    proc = run_cli(exe, ["doctor", "--agent"])
    try:
        doc = json.loads(proc.stdout)
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        die(4, f"doctor output was not JSON (exit {proc.returncode}): "
               f"{proc.stdout[:200]} {proc.stderr[:200]}")
    if doc.get("auth") != "configured":
        die(4, "Fireflies auth not configured. Set FIREFLIES_API_KEY in the "
               "environment (doctor reported auth="
               f"{doc.get('auth')!r}, source={doc.get('auth_source')!r}).")


def refresh_db(exe: str) -> None:
    """Step 2: pull any newly processed transcripts into the local DB."""
    proc = run_cli(exe, ["sync", "--agent"], timeout=600)
    if proc.returncode != 0:
        die(3, f"fireflies-pp-cli sync failed (exit {proc.returncode}): "
               f"{proc.stderr.strip() or proc.stdout.strip()}")


def find_transcripts(exe: str, days_back: int) -> list:
    """Step 3: list processed transcripts in the lookback window."""
    proc = run_cli(exe, [
        "transcripts", "find", "--from", str(days_back),
        "--processed-only", "--json", "--agent",
        # CLI defaults to --limit 100, which silently truncates large
        # backfills (e.g. the 235-meeting ingest); override it.
        "--limit", "100000",
    ])
    if proc.returncode != 0:
        die(3, f"transcripts find failed (exit {proc.returncode}): "
               f"{proc.stderr.strip() or proc.stdout.strip()}")
    try:
        data = json.loads(proc.stdout)
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        die(3, f"transcripts find output was not JSON: {proc.stdout[:200]}")
    if isinstance(data, dict):
        for key in ("transcripts", "results", "items", "data"):
            if isinstance(data.get(key), list):
                data = data[key]
                break
        else:
            die(3, f"unrecognized find JSON shape: keys={list(data)[:10]}")
    if not isinstance(data, list):
        die(3, "transcripts find JSON is neither a list nor a known wrapper")
    return [t for t in data if isinstance(t, dict) and t.get("id")]


def load_state(state_path: Path) -> dict:
    """Step 4 support: load {"exports": {...}}; back up and recreate if corrupt."""
    if not state_path.exists():
        return {"exports": {}}
    try:
        with open(state_path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            state = json.load(f)
        if not isinstance(state, dict) or not isinstance(state.get("exports"), dict):
            raise ValueError("missing exports map")
        return state
    except (OSError, ValueError, json.JSONDecodeError) as e:
        bak = state_path.with_suffix(state_path.suffix + ".bak")
        shutil.copy2(state_path, bak)
        log(f"WARNING: state file corrupted ({e}); backed up to {bak.name}, "
            "starting fresh. This run may re-export (filenames are "
            "deterministic, so the filesystem stays idempotent).")
        return {"exports": {}}


def save_state(state_path: Path, state: dict) -> None:
    tmp = state_path.with_suffix(state_path.suffix + ".tmp")
    with open(tmp, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(state, f, indent=2)
    tmp.replace(state_path)


def transcript_date(t: dict) -> str:
    return str(t.get("dateString") or t.get("date") or "")


def export_new(exe: str, pending: list, vault: Path,
               state_path: Path, state: dict) -> list:
    """Step 5: export each pending transcript, detecting the written file by
    diffing the vault directory listing before/after each export (never
    "newest .md" — a no-op export must not claim an unrelated file)."""
    exported_paths = []
    for t in pending:
        tid = t["id"]
        before = {p.name for p in vault.glob("*.md")}
        proc = run_cli(exe, [
            "transcripts", "export", tid,
            "--vault", str(vault), "--agent",
        ], timeout=600)
        if proc.returncode != 0:
            log(f"WARNING: export failed for {tid} "
                f"(exit {proc.returncode}): "
                f"{proc.stderr.strip() or proc.stdout.strip()} — continuing.")
            continue
        new_files = [p for p in vault.glob("*.md") if p.name not in before]
        if not new_files:
            log(f"WARNING: export for {tid} reported success but no new file "
                "appeared in the vault; skipping state update to avoid "
                "tagging the wrong file.")
            continue
        if len(new_files) > 1:
            log(f"NOTE: export for {tid} produced {len(new_files)} new files; "
                "using the most recently written one.")
        exported = max(new_files, key=lambda p: p.stat().st_mtime)
        state["exports"][tid] = {
            "filename": exported.name,
            "exported_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
        }
        save_state(state_path, state)  # persist per-export: crash-safe
        exported_paths.append(str(exported))
        log(f"exported {tid} -> {exported.name}")
    return exported_paths


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="meeting-sync pipeline")
    parser.add_argument("--days-back", type=int, default=None,
                        help="lookback window in days (default: "
                             "meeting_lookback_days from shared config)")
    parser.add_argument("--list-only", action="store_true",
                        help="print pending (not-yet-exported) transcripts as "
                             "JSON [{id,title,date}] and exit without exporting")
    parser.add_argument("--no-sync", action="store_true",
                        help="skip the fireflies-pp-cli sync refresh (use when "
                             "a sync already ran moments ago, e.g. after "
                             "--list-only)")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    cfg = load_config()
    days_back = args.days_back or int(cfg.get("meeting_lookback_days", 14))
    vault_root = Path(cfg.get("vault_root", ""))
    if not vault_root.is_dir():
        die(2, f"configured vault_root does not exist: {vault_root}")
    vault = Path(cfg["vault_inbox_meetings"])
    state_path = Path(cfg["meeting_sync_state_file"])
    vault.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    exe = resolve_cli(cfg)
    check_auth(exe)
    if not args.no_sync:
        refresh_db(exe)
    transcripts = find_transcripts(exe, days_back)
    state = load_state(state_path)
    pending = [t for t in transcripts if t["id"] not in state["exports"]]
    log(f"{len(transcripts)} transcripts in last {days_back} days; "
        f"{len(pending)} not yet exported.")

    if args.list_only:
        print(json.dumps(
            [{"id": t["id"], "title": t.get("title", ""),
              "date": transcript_date(t)} for t in pending],
            indent=2))
        return 0

    exported = export_new(exe, pending, vault, state_path, state)
    print(json.dumps(exported, indent=2))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

4	  Sync new Fireflies transcripts into the SecondBrain vault; audit vault filenames for
5	  drift against Fireflies titles. Idempotent. Use when the user says "sync meetings",
6	  "pull latest meetings", "/meeting-sync", "update meeting notes", "any new meetings?",
7	  or when invoked by weekly-review. Also for filename drift — "are any meeting files
8	  misnamed?", "did a meeting get renamed after export?", "why is this meeting titled
9	  differently in Fireflies than in the vault?", "audit the meeting filenames". Do not
10	  use to rename generic titles inside Fireflies (use name-meetings) or to search what
11	  was said in transcripts (use pp-fireflies).
12	argument-hint: "[days-back]"
13	---
14	
15	# Meeting Sync
16	
17	Pull new Fireflies transcripts into the SecondBrain vault. Each meeting becomes one markdown file at `Inbox/meetings/YYYY-MM-DD_<title>.md`.
18	
19	## Paths — shared config
20	
21	Vault and state-file paths live in `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.<platform>.json` (single source of truth):
22	- `vault_inbox_meetings` — platform-specific export target
23	- `meeting_sync_state_file` — idempotency ledger (`.sync-state.json` in that folder)
24	- `meeting_lookback_days` — default window (14)
25	
26	`scripts/sync.py` reads these itself; don't hardcode paths elsewhere. If the vault ever moves, edit the config only.
27	
28	sync.py passes `--limit 100000` to `transcripts find` — the CLI's default is 100, which silently truncates large backfills. Don't remove that flag.
29	
30	## Prerequisite — one-time auth
31	
32	Auth is the `FIREFLIES_API_KEY` environment variable (see the `pp-fireflies` skill's Auth Setup). Verify with `fireflies-pp-cli doctor --agent` — the JSON must show `"auth": "configured"`. `scripts/sync.py` runs this check itself and exits with code 4 if auth is missing. In that case, stop and tell the user:
33	
34	> Fireflies isn't authenticated yet. On the Mac, store the key in the Keychain with `security add-generic-password -U -s FIREFLIES_API_KEY -a "$USER" -w` (it prompts for the key; `~/.zshrc` exports it); on Windows, set it under System Properties → Environment Variables. Then open a new terminal. After that, `/meeting-sync` will work.
35	
36	Do not try to fix auth yourself (no `auth set-token` — the env var is the canonical mechanism). Then exit.
37	
38	## Sync flow
39	
40	### 1. Run the pipeline script
41	
42	The deterministic pipeline (doctor check → CLI sync → find → state diff → export → state update) is fully implemented in `scripts/sync.py`. Two-phase invocation:
43	
44	**Phase A — list pending, check titles:**
45	```bash
46	python scripts/sync.py --list-only [--days-back N]
47	```
48	Prints a JSON array of not-yet-exported transcripts: `[{"id", "title", "date"}]`. Diagnostics go to stderr.
49	
50	**Phase B — export:**
51	```bash
52	python scripts/sync.py --no-sync [--days-back N]
53	```
54	Prints a JSON array of newly exported absolute file paths (`--no-sync` skips the redundant DB refresh Phase A just did). Exports are detected by diffing the vault directory listing before/after each export — never "most recent .md" — so a no-op export can't claim an unrelated file.
55	
56	`[days-back]` argument from the user maps to `--days-back N`; otherwise the config default applies.
57	
58	### 2. Between phases: generic-title judgment (model's job)
59	
60	The user does not name their Fireflies meetings consistently. Generic titles produce useless filenames in the vault. Check each pending `title` from Phase A against the generic patterns documented in the `name-meetings` skill (empty, `Zoom Meeting`, `Recording`, `Meeting`, date-only, etc.).
61	
62	- **0 generics:** run Phase B immediately, silently.
63	- **1–3 generics:** use `AskUserQuestion` once — question: "N of the new meetings have generic titles. Name them before exporting?" with options **[Propose names first / Export as-is]**. If "Propose names first", invoke the `name-meetings` skill scoped to just these IDs, then re-run Phase A to pick up renamed titles before Phase B.
64	- **4+ generics:** report the count and suggest: *"Several new meetings have generic titles. Run `/name-meetings` to clean them up — I'll proceed with the export either way."* Then run Phase B without blocking.
65	
66	This keeps the rename loop tight at sync-time without blocking the pipeline.
67	
68	### 3. Augment each exported file (model's job)
69	
70	For each path in Phase B's JSON output, the file is raw Fireflies markdown. Insert the fixed 5-section header from `assets/meeting-header.md` (this skill's folder) at the top — after frontmatter, before any existing content. Read the asset and prepend it verbatim.
71	
72	Leave the Fireflies-generated transcript and summary below this block intact. This gives the user **5 fixed sections to fill in or curate** during interview-me / weekly-review, on top of the raw Fireflies content.
73	
74	### 4. Tag each exported file with its project (script's job)
75	
76	After the header is in place, pass the same paths to the tagger:
77	
78	```bash
79	python scripts/tag_project.py <path> [<path> ...]
80	```
81	
82	It asks TypeSafe's Jev which `portfolio.json` project each meeting is mainly about, and adds `- project/<PortfolioName>` under `## Project tags` only when the answer is confident. It always adds one `<!-- jev-project: ... -->` line recording what was asked and answered, which is also how a rerun knows to skip the note. `meeting-prep` reads the `- project/` line to find a project's meetings.
83	
84	It never blocks the sync: no key, no network or no transcript just leaves the note untagged and logs to stderr. Relay any `WARNING` lines. Run it only after step 3, because notes without a `## Project tags` header are skipped.
85	
86	## Drift audit (periodic, not every sync)
87	
88	A vault filename is a snapshot of the Fireflies title at export time. Titles get renamed afterwards, so the two drift apart. `scripts/audit_filenames.py` detects this by asking the export CLI to regenerate every filename into a scratch dir and diffing against the ledger — **the slug algorithm is never reimplemented**, the CLI is the authority.
89	
90	```bash
91	python scripts/audit_filenames.py [--since YYYY-MM-DD] [--skip-linkcheck] [--report PATH]
92	```
93	
94	Run it from `weekly-review`, or on demand — **not** on every sync (it spawns one CLI call per ledger entry, ~2-4 min for a full vault). Same exit codes as sync.py; drift itself is not an error, read the counts in the JSON.
95	
96	It classifies every mismatch, and the classes need different responses:
97	
98	- **`regression`** — the vault name is good and Fireflies has reverted to an auto-generated stamp (`Jan_19_0445_PM`, `Untitled`, `Audio_Message`). **Never re-export these — it destroys the good name.** Fix the title upstream in Fireflies instead. Note the API refuses title updates on some older meetings; if so, say so and leave the vault alone (the ledger already protects it).
99	- **`semantic`** — the title genuinely differs in meaning. Usually two generations of AI naming rather than rot, so it needs a human call, not an automatic rename. Surface it, don't act.
100	- **`cosmetic`** — same words, different separators (`RTP_UpperExtremity` vs `RTP___Upper_Extremity`). Ignore; re-exporting is pure churn.
101	
102	Before proposing any rename, check `inbound_links` in the output. Renaming a vault file breaks `[[wikilinks]]` from weekly-review notes and `GRAPH_REPORT.md`. Rewrite those links in the same pass or leave the file alone.
103	
104	## Output to user
105	
106	When done, report:
107	- N transcripts found in the window (stderr line from sync.py)
108	- M new exports written, K tagged with a project
109	- Path: `Inbox/meetings/`
110	- If 0 new: just say "No new meetings since last sync."
111	
112	Keep it to 3 lines.
113	
114	## Error handling
115	
116	sync.py exit codes: 0 ok, 2 usage/config, 3 sync/find failure, 4 auth not configured.
117	
118	- **Exit 4 (auth):** deliver the auth message from Prerequisite above, stop.
119	- **Exit 3 (sync/find):** report the stderr error verbatim, do not try to recover. The user may need to refresh their API key.
120	- **Export fails for one transcript:** sync.py logs a warning to stderr and continues with the rest; relay which one failed.
121	- **State file corrupted:** sync.py backs it up to `.sync-state.json.bak` and recreates fresh automatically (re-export is idempotent on the filesystem because filenames are deterministic per CLI); flag this in the report if the warning appears.
122	
123	## Gotchas
124	
125	- **Two tag vocabularies share `## Project tags`.** Hand tags are topic words (`project/rtp`, `project/load-monitoring`). Jev tags are exact `portfolio.json` names (`project/Sport_Tech_Vetting`). The tagger only appends and never edits or removes a hand tag.
126	- **Measured before shipping, so don't tune the question here.** The question wording and the 0.60 threshold in `tag_project.py` were tested blind on 40 meetings (TypeSafe_Sandbox `docs/FIREFLIES_PROJECT_TAG.md`, 2026-09-22). Jev was confident on 36, and right on 33 of those. It never confidently tagged a non-project meeting, but it found only 7 of 11 real project meetings. OKRs_2026-27 was the repeat miss. Judge any wording change against meetings the test didn't use.
127	- **A missing tag is not evidence the meeting is unrelated.** The marker line says `none of these` or `(unsure)`. Callers still fall back to text search.
128	- **Probabilities wobble by a few points between runs** (for example 0.83 vs 0.81 on the same note). Notes near 0.60 can go either way, which is one reason the marker is written once and not re-asked.
129	- **Vault notes can mix CRLF and LF lines.** The tagger splices in its lines and never re-encodes the file. Don't "clean up" line endings in this script: an earlier draft did, and rewrote about 50 lines of one note.
130	
131	## What NOT to do
132	
133	- **Don't re-implement steps the script owns** — doctor, CLI sync, find, state diff, export, state update all live in `scripts/sync.py`.
134	- **Don't identify exports by "newest .md file"** — that's the exact bug the directory-diff in sync.py fixes.
135	- **Don't detect filename drift by pattern-matching for "generic-looking" names** — that both misses real drift and invents fake drift. Use `audit_filenames.py`, which compares against what the export CLI actually produces.
136	- **Don't bulk re-export to "clean up" filenames.** Most mismatches are cosmetic or a second valid naming generation, and the `regression` class gets actively worse. Re-export only what a human approved.
137	- **Don't modify the Fireflies-generated content** of the exported file — only PREPEND the header from `assets/meeting-header.md`. The transcript and AI summary stay untouched.
138	- **Don't sync every interaction.** Run sync only when explicitly invoked OR when called by weekly-review / fireflies-intake.
139

14	
15	Replaces the recurring hand-typed sequence: "ingest my recent fireflies meetings" → "some have generic names, rename them" → "is everything from <date> in the second brain?" Runs the full chain in order, unattended, then reports.

Renaming BEFORE sync means the vault notes are created under their proper names — no cleanup pass later.

25	## Step 2 — Sync
26	
27	Invoke the **meeting-sync** skill to pull all transcripts not yet in the SecondBrain vault. It is idempotent — run it over the full recent window rather than trying to compute the delta yourself.
28	
29	## Step 3 — Verify completeness
30	
31	Compare the Fireflies meeting list for the sync window against the vault's meeting notes (the pp-fireflies CLI's local database is the cheapest source for the meeting list; the vault folder is `vault_inbox_meetings` and the export ledger is `meeting_sync_state_file`, both in `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.<platform>.json`). Every meeting must be accounted for: ingested now, ingested previously, or intentionally skipped (with the reason).

34

38	**Renamed:** <n> meetings (<old → new>, one line each; or "none needed")
39	**Ingested:** <n> new meetings → <vault folder path>
40	   - <meeting name> (<date>)
41	**Already in vault:** <n>
42	**Skipped/failed:** <list with reasons, or "none">
43	**Queued for review:** <n> low-confidence rename proposals in .pending-renames.json (omit line if 0)
44	```
45	
46	If the user also wants the new notes graphed into the knowledge graph, they'll say so — offer `/graphify` as a one-line follow-up only when new meetings were actually ingested.
47	
48	## Rules
49	
50	- Never duplicate a vault note; trust meeting-sync's idempotency and say "already in vault" rather than re-ingesting.
51	- If the Fireflies API or CLI auth fails, report which step failed and stop — don't half-ingest silently.
52	- An empty run is a valid result: "No new meetings since <date>" is the complete report.

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""meeting-sync deterministic pipeline (steps 1-5 of SKILL.md).
3	
4	Pipeline: doctor auth check -> fireflies-pp-cli sync -> transcripts find
5	-> state-file diff -> export loop (directory-diff file detection)
6	-> state-file update.
7	
8	stdout: a JSON array. Full run: absolute paths of newly exported .md files.
9	--list-only: pending (not-yet-exported) transcripts as
10	{"id", "title", "date"} objects, no export performed.
11	All diagnostics go to stderr.
12	
13	Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 unexpected, 2 usage/config, 3 sync/find failure,
14	4 auth not configured.
15	
16	Paths come from the platform-specific shared config at ../../_shared/.
17	(vault_inbox_meetings, meeting_sync_state_file, meeting_lookback_days).
18	"""
19	
20	import argparse
21	import json
22	import shutil
23	import subprocess
24	import sys
25	from datetime import datetime, timezone
26	from pathlib import Path
27	
28	CONFIG_PATH = (
29	    Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
30	    / "_shared"
31	    / ("config.windows.json" if sys.platform == "win32" else "config.macos.json")
32	)
33	
34	
35	def log(msg: str) -> None:
36	    print(msg, file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
37	
38	
39	def die(code: int, msg: str) -> "None":
40	    log(f"ERROR: {msg}")
41	    sys.exit(code)
42	
43	
44	def load_config() -> dict:
45	    try:
46	        with open(CONFIG_PATH, encoding="utf-8") as f:
47	            cfg = json.load(f)
48	    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as e:
49	        die(2, f"cannot read shared config {CONFIG_PATH}: {e}")
50	    for key in ("vault_root", "vault_inbox_meetings", "meeting_sync_state_file"):
51	        if key not in cfg:
52	            die(2, f"shared config missing required key: {key}")
53	    return cfg
54	
55	
56	def resolve_cli(cfg: dict) -> str:
57	    configured = cfg.get("fireflies_cli")
58	    if configured and Path(configured).is_file():
59	        return str(configured)
60	    exe = shutil.which("fireflies-pp-cli")
61	    if not exe:
62	        die(2, "fireflies-pp-cli not found on PATH")
63	    return exe
64	
65	
66	def run_cli(exe: str, args: list, timeout: int = 300) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
67	    return subprocess.run(
68	        [exe] + args, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout
69	    )
70	
71	
72	def check_auth(exe: str) -> None:
73	    """Step 1: doctor. Requires JSON field "auth": "configured"
74	    (key comes from the FIREFLIES_API_KEY environment variable)."""
75	    proc = run_cli(exe, ["doctor", "--agent"])
76	    try:
77	        doc = json.loads(proc.stdout)
78	    except json.JSONDecodeError:
79	        die(4, f"doctor output was not JSON (exit {proc.returncode}): "
80	               f"{proc.stdout[:200]} {proc.stderr[:200]}")
81	    if doc.get("auth") != "configured":
82	        die(4, "Fireflies auth not configured. Set FIREFLIES_API_KEY in the "
83	               "environment (doctor reported auth="
84	               f"{doc.get('auth')!r}, source={doc.get('auth_source')!r}).")
85	
86	
87	def refresh_db(exe: str) -> None:
88	    """Step 2: pull any newly processed transcripts into the local DB."""
89	    proc = run_cli(exe, ["sync", "--agent"], timeout=600)
90	    if proc.returncode != 0:
91	        die(3, f"fireflies-pp-cli sync failed (exit {proc.returncode}): "
92	               f"{proc.stderr.strip() or proc.stdout.strip()}")
93	
94	
95	def find_transcripts(exe: str, days_back: int) -> list:
96	    """Step 3: list processed transcripts in the lookback window."""
97	    proc = run_cli(exe, [
98	        "transcripts", "find", "--from", str(days_back),
99	        "--processed-only", "--json", "--agent",
100	        # CLI defaults to --limit 100, which silently truncates large
101	        # backfills (e.g. the 235-meeting ingest); override it.
102	        "--limit", "100000",
103	    ])
104	    if proc.returncode != 0:
105	        die(3, f"transcripts find failed (exit {proc.returncode}): "
106	               f"{proc.stderr.strip() or proc.stdout.strip()}")
107	    try:
108	        data = json.loads(proc.stdout)
109	    except json.JSONDecodeError:
110	        die(3, f"transcripts find output was not JSON: {proc.stdout[:200]}")
111	    if isinstance(data, dict):
112	        for key in ("transcripts", "results", "items", "data"):
113	            if isinstance(data.get(key), list):
114	                data = data[key]
115	                break
116	        else:
117	            die(3, f"unrecognized find JSON shape: keys={list(data)[:10]}")
118	    if not isinstance(data, list):
119	        die(3, "transcripts find JSON is neither a list nor a known wrapper")
120	    return [t for t in data if isinstance(t, dict) and t.get("id")]
121	
122	
123	def load_state(state_path: Path) -> dict:
124	    """Step 4 support: load {"exports": {...}}; back up and recreate if corrupt."""
125	    if not state_path.exists():
126	        return {"exports": {}}
127	    try:
128	        with open(state_path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
129	            state = json.load(f)
130	        if not isinstance(state, dict) or not isinstance(state.get("exports"), dict):
131	            raise ValueError("missing exports map")
132	        return state
133	    except (OSError, ValueError, json.JSONDecodeError) as e:
134	        bak = state_path.with_suffix(state_path.suffix + ".bak")
135	        shutil.copy2(state_path, bak)
136	        log(f"WARNING: state file corrupted ({e}); backed up to {bak.name}, "
137	            "starting fresh. This run may re-export (filenames are "
138	            "deterministic, so the filesystem stays idempotent).")
139	        return {"exports": {}}
140	
141	
142	def save_state(state_path: Path, state: dict) -> None:
143	    tmp = state_path.with_suffix(state_path.suffix + ".tmp")
144	    with open(tmp, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
145	        json.dump(state, f, indent=2)
146	    tmp.replace(state_path)
147	
148	
149	def transcript_date(t: dict) -> str:
150	    return str(t.get("dateString") or t.get("date") or "")
151	
152	
153	def export_new(exe: str, pending: list, vault: Path,
154	               state_path: Path, state: dict) -> list:
155	    """Step 5: export each pending transcript, detecting the written file by
156	    diffing the vault directory listing before/after each export (never
157	    "newest .md" — a no-op export must not claim an unrelated file)."""
158	    exported_paths = []
159	    for t in pending:
160	        tid = t["id"]
161	        before = {p.name for p in vault.glob("*.md")}
162	        proc = run_cli(exe, [
163	            "transcripts", "export", tid,
164	            "--vault", str(vault), "--agent",
165	        ], timeout=600)
166	        if proc.returncode != 0:
167	            log(f"WARNING: export failed for {tid} "
168	                f"(exit {proc.returncode}): "
169	                f"{proc.stderr.strip() or proc.stdout.strip()} — continuing.")
170	            continue
171	        new_files = [p for p in vault.glob("*.md") if p.name not in before]
172	        if not new_files:
173	            log(f"WARNING: export for {tid} reported success but no new file "
174	                "appeared in the vault; skipping state update to avoid "
175	                "tagging the wrong file.")
176	            continue
177	        if len(new_files) > 1:
178	            log(f"NOTE: export for {tid} produced {len(new_files)} new files; "
179	                "using the most recently written one.")
180	        exported = max(new_files, key=lambda p: p.stat().st_mtime)
181	        state["exports"][tid] = {
182	            "filename": exported.name,
183	            "exported_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
184	        }
185	        save_state(state_path, state)  # persist per-export: crash-safe
186	        exported_paths.append(str(exported))
187	        log(f"exported {tid} -> {exported.name}")
188	    return exported_paths
189	
190	
191	def main() -> int:
192	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="meeting-sync pipeline")
193	    parser.add_argument("--days-back", type=int, default=None,
194	                        help="lookback window in days (default: "
195	                             "meeting_lookback_days from shared config)")
196	    parser.add_argument("--list-only", action="store_true",
197	                        help="print pending (not-yet-exported) transcripts as "
198	                             "JSON [{id,title,date}] and exit without exporting")
199	    parser.add_argument("--no-sync", action="store_true",
200	                        help="skip the fireflies-pp-cli sync refresh (use when "
201	                             "a sync already ran moments ago, e.g. after "
202	                             "--list-only)")
203	    args = parser.parse_args()
204	
205	    cfg = load_config()
206	    days_back = args.days_back or int(cfg.get("meeting_lookback_days", 14))
207	    vault_root = Path(cfg.get("vault_root", ""))
208	    if not vault_root.is_dir():
209	        die(2, f"configured vault_root does not exist: {vault_root}")
210	    vault = Path(cfg["vault_inbox_meetings"])
211	    state_path = Path(cfg["meeting_sync_state_file"])
212	    vault.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
213	
214	    exe = resolve_cli(cfg)
215	    check_auth(exe)
216	    if not args.no_sync:
217	        refresh_db(exe)
218	    transcripts = find_transcripts(exe, days_back)
219	    state = load_state(state_path)
220	    pending = [t for t in transcripts if t["id"] not in state["exports"]]
221	    log(f"{len(transcripts)} transcripts in last {days_back} days; "
222	        f"{len(pending)} not yet exported.")
223	
224	    if args.list_only:
225	        print(json.dumps(
226	            [{"id": t["id"], "title": t.get("title", ""),
227	              "date": transcript_date(t)} for t in pending],
228	            indent=2))
229	        return 0
230	
231	    exported = export_new(exe, pending, vault, state_path, state)
232	    print(json.dumps(exported, indent=2))
233	    return 0
234	
235	
236	if __name__ == "__main__":
237	    sys.exit(main())

$fn = $ast.FindAll({ $args[0] -is [System.Management.Automation.Language.FunctionDefinitionAst] -and $args[0].Name -eq 'Test-GenericMeetingTitle' }, $true) | Select-Object -First 1

. ([scriptblock]::Create($fn.Extent.Text))

---
name: meeting-sync
description: >-
  Engine that turns Fireflies transcripts into SecondBrain meeting notes: renames
  generic titles, exports new meetings, tags each note with its portfolio project.
  Use when the user says "/meeting-sync", or when invoked by weekly-review or
  fireflies-intake. Also for filename drift: "are any meeting files misnamed?", "audit
  the meeting filenames". Do not use for "ingest my meetings" requests (use
  fireflies-intake), renaming titles by hand (use name-meetings), or searching what was
  said (use pp-fireflies).
argument-hint: "[days-back]"
---

# Meeting Sync

One vault note per meeting at `Inbox/meetings/YYYY-MM-DD_<title>.md`, tagged with its project.

**Two exporters share one ledger.** The KeystoneOS 06:00 job (`keystone.ps1 meeting-sync`) exports every new meeting that has a real title, with its own header and keyword tags, and leaves generic titles unexported. So this skill's work is: rename and export the generic ones, then add the Jev project tag to every note in the window. Both write `.sync-state.json`, so a meeting either one exported is done for both.

Paths (`vault_inbox_meetings`, `meeting_sync_state_file`, `meeting_lookback_days`, default 14) live in `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.<platform>.json`; the scripts read them. Below, `S=~/.claude/skills/meeting-sync/scripts`.

## Steps

1. **List pending.** `python3 $S/sync.py --list-only [--days-back N]` checks auth, refreshes the Fireflies DB, and prints `[{"id","title","date"}]` for transcripts not in the ledger. Its stderr line "N transcripts in last D days; M not yet exported" goes in the report. Exit 4 is auth: give the **Auth** message and stop. Exit 3: report stderr verbatim and stop. Other codes are in the script's docstring.
2. **Rename generic titles.** Check each pending title against `~/.claude/skills/name-meetings/REFERENCE.md` → Generic-title patterns. If any match, invoke `name-meetings` in **Unattended mode** (declare it), scoped to those ids: HIGH-confidence renames are applied, the rest go to `review[]` in the pending-renames file. Then re-run step 1.
3. **Export.** `python3 $S/sync.py --no-sync [--days-back N]` prints the new file paths. A meeting still generic after step 2 exports as it is and is named in the report.
4. **Add the header** to each step 3 path: prepend `~/.claude/skills/meeting-sync/assets/meeting-header.md` verbatim at the top. The Fireflies content below stays as it is. Notes from the 06:00 job already carry their own header.
5. **Tag the window.** Pass every note dated in the window, from both exporters, to the tagger:
   ```bash
   python3 -c "import glob,json,os,datetime as d; v=json.load(open(os.path.expanduser('~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.macos.json')))['vault_inbox_meetings']; cut=(d.date.today()-d.timedelta(days=14)).isoformat(); print('\n'.join(p for p in sorted(glob.glob(v+'/20*.md')) if os.path.basename(p)[:10]>=cut))" | xargs python3 $S/tag_project.py
   ```
   It skips notes that already hold a `<!-- jev-project:` marker or have no `## Project tags` header. For the rest it sends the Fireflies summary to TypeSafe's Jev (the flow Eric set up 2026-09-22), adds `- project/<PortfolioName>` when Jev is confident (≥ 0.60), and always writes one marker line. No key, no network or no transcript leaves a note untagged: relay each `WARNING` line.
6. **Report**, three lines: transcripts in the window, new exports and notes tagged; renames applied, queued for review, and any still-generic titles; the path `Inbox/meetings/`. With nothing new and nothing to tag: "No new meetings since last sync."

**Done when** every transcript in the window is in the ledger or named as a failed export, every note in the window has a `jev-project` marker or a relayed WARNING, and the report names every generic title left.

## Auth

Auth is the `FIREFLIES_API_KEY` environment variable. On exit 4, stop and tell the user:

> Fireflies isn't authenticated yet. On the Mac, store the key in the Keychain with `security add-generic-password -U -s FIREFLIES_API_KEY -a "$USER" -w` (it prompts for the key; `~/.zshrc` exports it). Then open a new terminal. After that, `/meeting-sync` will work.

The env var is the one mechanism: leave `auth set-token` alone.

## What the scripts own

- `sync.py` does the doctor check, CLI sync, find (with `--limit 100000`; the CLI default of 100 truncates backfills), ledger diff, export and ledger update. It finds each export by diffing the folder listing before and after, so a no-op export never claims another file. One failed export is logged and the rest continue: relay which. A corrupt ledger is backed up to `.sync-state.json.bak` and rebuilt (filenames are deterministic, so re-export is safe): flag the warning.
- The Fireflies transcript and summary below the header are the record: edits go only in the header sections.

## Tagger facts

- **Two tag vocabularies share `## Project tags`.** Hand and 06:00-job tags are topic words (`project/rtp`). Jev tags are exact `portfolio.json` names (`project/Sport_Tech_Vetting`). The tagger only appends.
- **The wording and the 0.60 threshold were measured** blind on 40 meetings (TypeSafe_Sandbox `docs/FIREFLIES_PROJECT_TAG.md`, 2026-09-22): confident on 36, right on 33, never confidently wrong on a non-project meeting, but found only 7 of 11 real project meetings (OKRs_2026-27 the repeat miss). Judge any wording change against meetings that test did not use.
- **A missing tag is not evidence the meeting is unrelated.** The marker says `none of these` or `(unsure)`; callers still fall back to text search. Probabilities wobble a few points between runs, which is why the marker is written once and never re-asked.
- **Vault notes can mix CRLF and LF.** The tagger splices lines in and never re-encodes; an earlier draft that normalized line endings rewrote ~50 lines of one note.

## Filename drift audit

Weekly, from weekly-review, or when asked whether meeting files are misnamed: follow `DRIFT.md` (beside this file).

input.content:
# Filename drift audit

A vault filename is a snapshot of the Fireflies title at export time. Titles get renamed afterwards, so the two drift apart. `audit_filenames.py` asks the export CLI to regenerate every filename into a scratch folder and diffs against the ledger: the CLI is the authority on slugs, so the slug algorithm is never reimplemented, and drift is never guessed from "generic-looking" names.

```bash
python3 ~/.claude/skills/meeting-sync/scripts/audit_filenames.py [--since YYYY-MM-DD] [--skip-linkcheck] [--report PATH]
```

One CLI call per ledger entry (~2-4 min for the full vault), so it runs weekly, not on every sync. Same exit codes as `sync.py`; drift itself is not an error, read the counts in the JSON.

Each class needs a different response:

- **`regression`**: the vault name is good and Fireflies reverted to an auto-generated stamp (`Jan_19_0445_PM`, `Untitled`, `Audio_Message`). Fix the title upstream in Fireflies; re-exporting would destroy the good name. The API refuses title updates on some older meetings: say so and leave the vault alone (the ledger protects it).
- **`semantic`**: the title differs in meaning, usually two generations of AI naming. Surface it for a human call.
- **`cosmetic`**: same words, different separators (`RTP_UpperExtremity` vs `RTP___Upper_Extremity`). Ignore.

Re-export or rename only what Eric approved. Before any rename, check `inbound_links` in the output: renaming a vault file breaks `[[wikilinks]]` from weekly-review notes and `GRAPH_REPORT.md`, so rewrite those links in the same pass or leave the file alone.

# Meeting Sync

One vault note per meeting at `Inbox/meetings/YYYY-MM-DD_<title>.md`, tagged with its project.

**Two exporters share one ledger.** The KeystoneOS 06:00 job (`keystone.ps1 meeting-sync`) exports every new meeting that has a real title, with its own header and keyword tags, and leaves generic titles unexported. So this skill's work is: rename and export the generic ones, then add the Jev project tag to every note in the window. Both write `.sync-state.json`, so a meeting either one exported is done for both.

Paths (`vault_inbox_meetings`, `meeting_sync_state_file`, `meeting_lookback_days`, default 14) live in `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.<platform>.json`; the scripts read them. Below, `S=~/.claude/skills/meeting-sync/scripts`.

## Steps

1. **List pending.** `python3 $S/sync.py --list-only [--days-back N]` checks auth, refreshes the Fireflies DB, and prints `[{"id","title","date"}]` for transcripts not in the ledger. Its stderr line "N transcripts in last D days; M not yet exported" goes in the report. Exit 4 is auth: give the **Auth** message and stop. Exit 3: report stderr verbatim and stop. Other codes are in the script's docstring.
2. **Rename generic titles.** Check each pending title against `~/.claude/skills/name-meetings/REFERENCE.md` → Generic-title patterns. If any match, invoke `name-meetings` in **Unattended mode** (declare it), scoped to those ids: HIGH-confidence renames are applied, the rest go to `review[]` in the pending-renames file. Then re-run step 1.
3. **Export.** `python3 $S/sync.py --no-sync [--days-back N]` prints the new file paths. A meeting still generic after step 2 exports as it is and is named in the report.
4. **Add the header** to each step 3 path: prepend `~/.claude/skills/meeting-sync/assets/meeting-header.md` verbatim at the top. The Fireflies content below stays as it is. Notes from the 06:00 job already carry their own header.
5. **Tag the window.** Pass every note dated in the window, from both exporters, to the tagger:
   ```bash
   python3 -c "import glob,json,os,datetime as d; v=json.load(open(os.path.expanduser('~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.macos.json')))['vault_inbox_meetings']; cut=(d.date.today()-d.timedelta(days=14)).isoformat(); print('\n'.join(p for p in sorted(glob.glob(v+'/20*.md')) if os.path.basename(p)[:10]>=cut))" | xargs python3 $S/tag_project.py
   ```
   It skips notes that already hold a `<!-- jev-project:` marker or have no `## Project tags` header. For the rest it sends the Fireflies summary to TypeSafe's Jev (the flow Eric set up 2026-09-22), adds `- project/<PortfolioName>` when Jev is confident (≥ 0.60), and always writes one marker line. No key, no network or no transcript leaves a note untagged: relay each `WARNING` line.
6. **Report**, three lines: transcripts in the window, new exports and notes tagged; renames applied, queued for review, and any still-generic titles; the path `Inbox/meetings/`. With nothing new and nothing to tag: "No new meetings since last sync."

**Done when** every transcript in the window is in the ledger or named as a failed export, every note in the window has a `jev-project` marker or a relayed WARNING, and the report names every generic title left.

## Auth

Auth is the `FIREFLIES_API_KEY` environment variable. On exit 4, stop and tell the user:

> Fireflies isn't authenticated yet. On the Mac, store the key in the Keychain with `security add-generic-password -U -s FIREFLIES_API_KEY -a "$USER" -w` (it prompts for the key; `~/.zshrc` exports it). Then open a new terminal. After that, `/meeting-sync` will work.

The env var is the one mechanism: leave `auth set-token` alone.

## What the scripts own

- `sync.py` does the doctor check, CLI sync, find (with `--limit 100000`; the CLI default of 100 truncates backfills), ledger diff, export and ledger update. It finds each export by diffing the folder listing before and after, so a no-op export never claims another file. One failed export is logged and the rest continue: relay which. A corrupt ledger is backed up to `.sync-state.json.bak` and rebuilt (filenames are deterministic, so re-export is safe): flag the warning.
- The Fireflies transcript and summary below the header are the record: edits go only in the header sections.

## Tagger facts

- **Two tag vocabularies share `## Project tags`.** Hand and 06:00-job tags are topic words (`project/rtp`). Jev tags are exact `portfolio.json` names (`project/Sport_Tech_Vetting`). The tagger only appends.
- **The wording and the 0.60 threshold were measured** blind on 40 meetings (TypeSafe_Sandbox `docs/FIREFLIES_PROJECT_TAG.md`, 2026-09-22): confident on 36, right on 33, never confidently wrong on a non-project meeting, but found only 7 of 11 real project meetings (OKRs_2026-27 the repeat miss). Judge any wording change against meetings that test did not use.
- **A missing tag is not evidence the meeting is unrelated.** The marker says `none of these` or `(unsure)`; callers still fall back to text search. Probabilities wobble a few points between runs, which is why the marker is written once and never re-asked.
- **Vault notes can mix CRLF and LF.** The tagger splices lines in and never re-encodes; an earlier draft that normalized line endings rewrote ~50 lines of one note.

Reference for writing any document an agent consumes: a skill, an `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md`, a doc reached by a pointer. The packaging differs; the writing does not: the same levers make each one predictable, since the agent takes the same _process_ every run rather than producing the same output.

When the document you're writing is a skill, read [`SKILL-MECHANICS.md`](SKILL-MECHANICS.md) for frontmatter, invocation choice, and router skills.

## Context pointers

A **context pointer** is a reference held in the agent's context that names some out-of-context material and encodes the condition for reaching it. A skill's description is one; a line in `AGENTS.md` naming a doc is the same object. The pointer's _wording_, not its target, decides when the agent reaches the material, and how reliably. A must-have target behind a weakly worded pointer is a variance bug: sharpen the wording first, and inline the material only if sharpening fails.

A pointer does two jobs: state what the material is, and list the **branches** that should trigger reaching it (a branch is a distinct case the document handles, so different runs take different paths through it). Every word of an always-loaded pointer costs on every turn, so it earns even harder pruning than the body:

- **Front-load the leading word**: the pointer is where it does its triggering work.
- **One trigger per branch.** Synonyms that rename a single branch are one branch written twice; collapse them and keep only genuinely distinct branches.
- **Cut identity the body already carries.**

## The two loads

Every document and pointer you add spends one of two budgets:

- **Context load** is the cost of always-loaded material on the agent's window: an `AGENTS.md` line, a skill description, anything sitting in context every turn, spending tokens and attention whether or not it fires.
- **Cognitive load** is the cost on the human: which documents exist and when to reach for each. The human is the index. Not a cost to minimise: it is the price of human agency; spend it where human judgement matters, remove it where it does not.

Material reached only through a pointer escapes context load at the price of the pointer's own line; material with no pointer at all rides entirely on cognitive load.

## Information hierarchy

A document is built from two content types: **steps** (the ordered actions the agent performs) and **reference** (definitions, rules, facts consulted on demand). The two mix freely: all steps (a recipe), all reference (a review's rules, this skill), or both. The core decision is where each piece sits on the **information hierarchy**, a ladder ranked by how immediately the agent needs the material:

1. **In-file step** is the primary tier: what the agent does, in order.
2. **In-file reference** is consulted on demand. Often a legitimately flat peer-set (every rule of a review on one rung), which is a fine arrangement, not a smell.
3. **Disclosed reference** is pushed out into a separate file, reached by a context pointer, loaded only when the pointer fires. Spans a sibling file in the same folder through fully external reference that lives anywhere and any document can point at.

Push too little down and the top bloats; push too much and you hide material the agent actually needs. That tension is the whole decision.

**Progressive disclosure** is the move down the ladder (out of the main file and behind a pointer) so the top stays legible. Not primarily a token optimisation: it is how the hierarchy is protected. Branching is the cleanest disclosure test: inline what every branch needs, and push behind a pointer what only some branches reach. When a document has steps, in-file reference that should be disclosed buries them and turns attending to them into a coin-flip: a variance lever, not just a legibility one.

**Co-location** is the within-file companion: where the ladder decides _how far down_ a piece sits, co-location decides _what sits beside it_ once there. Keep a concept's definition, rules, and caveats under one heading rather than scattered, so reading one part brings its neighbours with it. The test: the document should read like documentation written for the agent. Grouped material reads that way; scattered material does not. (Distinct from duplication: that repeats one meaning in two places; scattering fragments one meaning across many.)

**Sprawl** is the failure mode here: a document simply too long, even when every line is live and unique. Attention thins across the excess, and every extra line is one more to keep relevant. The cure is the ladder: disclose reference behind pointers, and split by branch or sequence so each path carries only what it needs.

## Steps and completion criteria

Every step ends on a **completion criterion**, the condition that tells the agent the work is done. Two properties make it a lever:

- **Clarity**: can the agent tell done from not-done? A vague bound ("understanding reached") invites **premature completion**: ending the step before it is genuinely done, attention slipping to _being done_. The visible steps still ahead (the **post-completion steps**) supply the pull; the criterion's clarity is the resistance. Defend in order: **sharpen the bound first** (local and cheap); only if it is irreducibly fuzzy _and_ you observe the rush, hide the later steps by splitting the sequence. Hiding only works across a real context boundary (a hand-off or a subagent dispatch; an inline call leaves the later steps in context and clears nothing).
- **Demand**: how much it requires. "Every modified model accounted for" forces thorough work where "produce a change list" does not. Demand drives **legwork** (the digging the agent does within the work, latent in the wording rather than written as its own step), and it is not step-bound: "every rule applied" binds a body of flat reference just as "every step done" binds a sequence, which is how an all-reference document still carries an exhaustiveness bar.

The strongest criteria are both checkable and exhaustive.

## When to split

Splitting one document into two spends one of the two loads, so split only when the cut earns it:

- **By sequence**: split a run of steps where the post-completion steps tempt the agent to rush the one in front of it. Keeping them out of view drives more legwork on the current task. Beware the reverse: merging sequences exposes each step's later steps to what follows, inviting premature completion.
- **By invocation**, skill-specific: see [`SKILL-MECHANICS.md`](SKILL-MECHANICS.md).

## Leading words

A **leading word** is a compact concept already living in the model's pretraining that the agent thinks with while running the document (_lesson_, _fog of war_, _tracer bullets_). Repeated as a token, never as a sentence, it accumulates a distributed definition and anchors a whole region of behaviour in the fewest tokens, by recruiting priors the model already holds. Coining your own works if you define it clearly, but a made-up word recruits no priors: you pay in definition tokens what a pretrained word gives free; reach for an existing word first.

It anchors twice. In the body, _execution_: the agent reaches for the same behaviour every time the word appears, and inside flat reference it focuses attention on a class of thing to look for. In a pointer, _invocation_: when the same word lives in your prompts, your docs, and your codebase, the agent links that shared language to the material and reaches it more reliably.

Hunt for opportunities to refactor with leading words. A triad spelled out at three sites, a pointer spending a sentence to gesture at one idea. Each is a passage begging to collapse into a single token:

- "fast, deterministic, low-overhead" → _tight_ (a _tight_ loop).
- "a loop you believe in" → _red_, turning a fuzzy gate into a binary observable state (the loop goes _red_ on the bug, or it doesn't).

You win twice: fewer tokens, and a sharper hook for the agent to hang its thinking on. Assume every document is carrying restatements that leading words retire. Go find them.

**Negation** is the failure mode beside this lever: steering by prohibition drags the forbidden behaviour into context and makes it _more_ available, not less. _Don't think of an elephant_, and the elephant is all there is; the negation is a weak modifier the strongly-activated concept overruns, so the ban half-reads as an instruction to do the thing. Prompt the **positive**: state the target behaviour ("write one-line comments") so the banned one is never spoken. A prohibition earns its place only as a hard guardrail you cannot phrase positively; even then, pair it with the positive target so attention lands on what to do.

## Pruning

- Keep each meaning in a **single source of truth**: one authoritative place, so changing the behaviour is a one-place edit. **Duplication** (the same meaning in more than one place) costs maintenance and tokens, and inflates a meaning's prominence on the ladder past its real rank. (The accidental inverse of a leading word, which repeats a token on purpose, never the meaning.)
- The **environment** is a source of truth too (`package.json` scripts, config files, the directory layout, `--help` output), and a document that restates it is a **cache**: a copy of a lookup, earning its load only when the lookup is expensive. Cache what the agent cannot find by looking: the unwritten convention, the reason behind a choice, the gotcha no config confesses. Leave the one-file, one-command lookups to the environment, where they cannot go stale.
- Check every line for **relevance**: does it still bear on what the document does? A line loses relevance by never bearing on the task (mere exposition, or a branch that should be disclosed) or by going stale as the behaviour or world it describes changes. Shorter documents are easier to keep relevant. Without a pruning discipline the default fate is **sediment**: stale layers that settle because adding feels safe and removing feels risky, until you must core down through them to find what is still live.
- Hunt **no-ops** sentence by sentence: an instruction the model already obeys by default pays load to say nothing. The test (does it change behaviour versus the default?) is model-relative, not reader-relative: two people disagreeing about a no-op disagree about the default, and settle it by running the document, not by debate. When a sentence fails, delete the whole sentence rather than trim words from it. The test also grades leading words: a word too weak to beat the default (_be thorough_ when the agent is already thorough-ish) is a no-op, and the fix is a stronger word (_relentless_), not a different technique.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""meeting-sync step 4: tag each exported meeting note with its portfolio project (Jev).

For every note path given, looks up the Fireflies transcript through the sync ledger,
asks TypeSafe's Jev one Choice ("which portfolio project is this meeting mainly about,
or none of these"), and edits only the note's `## Project tags` section:

- confident (top probability >= 0.60) and a project -> adds `- project/<Name>`
- confident "none", or not confident                 -> adds no tag
- either way, adds one `<!-- jev-project: ... -->` line, so a rerun skips the note

Existing tags are never changed or removed. If Jev or the transcript is unavailable,
the note is left untouched (no marker), so a later run retries it. Always exits 0 on
per-note failures: tagging must never block a sync.

The question wording and the 0.60 threshold are the ones measured blind against Eric's
labels on 40 meetings (TypeSafe_Sandbox docs/FIREFLIES_PROJECT_TAG.md, PR #23):
33 of 36 confident answers right. Change them there first, not here.

Usage:
    python scripts/tag_project.py PATH [PATH ...] [--dry-run]

stdout: JSON array of {"path", "choice", "p", "tag"}; diagnostics to stderr.
Exit codes: 0 ok, 2 usage/config.
"""

--- sync.py doc

"""meeting-sync deterministic pipeline (steps 1-5 of SKILL.md).

The env var is the one mechanism: leave `auth set-token` alone.

## What the scripts own

- `sync.py` does the doctor check, CLI sync, find (with `--limit 100000`; the CLI default of 100 truncates backfills), ledger diff, export and ledger update. It finds each export by diffing the folder listing before and after, so a no-op export never claims another file. One failed export is logged and the rest continue: relay which. A corrupt ledger is backed up to `.sync-state.json.bak` and rebuilt (filenames are deterministic, so re-export is safe): flag the warning.
- The Fireflies transcript and summary below the header are the record: edits go only in the header sections.

## Tagger facts

- **Two tag vocabularies share `## Project tags`.** Hand and 06:00-job tags are topic words (`project/rtp`). Jev tags are exact `portfolio.json` names (`project/Sport_Tech_Vetting`). The tagger only appends.
- **The wording and the 0.60 threshold were measured** blind on 40 meetings (TypeSafe_Sandbox `docs/FIREFLIES_PROJECT_TAG.md`, 2026-09-22): confident on 36, right on 33, never confidently wrong on a non-project meeting, but found only 7 of 11 real project meetings (OKRs_2026-27 the repeat miss). Judge any wording change against meetings that test did not use.
- **A missing tag is not evidence the meeting is unrelated.** The marker says `none of these` or `(unsure)`; callers still fall back to text search. Probabilities wobble a few points between runs, which is why the marker is written once and never re-asked.
- **Vault notes can mix CRLF and LF.** The tagger splices lines in and never re-encodes; an earlier draft that normalized line endings rewrote ~50 lines of one note.

# Meeting Sync

One vault note per meeting at `Inbox/meetings/YYYY-MM-DD_<title>.md`, tagged with its project.

**Two exporters share one ledger.** The KeystoneOS 06:00 job (`keystone.ps1 meeting-sync`) exports every new meeting that has a real title, with its own header and keyword tags, and leaves generic titles unexported. So this skill's work is: rename and export the generic ones, then add the Jev project tag to every note in the window. Both write `.sync-state.json`, so a meeting either one exported is done for both.

Paths (`vault_inbox_meetings`, `meeting_sync_state_file`, `meeting_lookback_days`, default 14) live in `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.<platform>.json`; the scripts read them. Below, `S=~/.claude/skills/meeting-sync/scripts`.

## Steps

1. **List pending.** `python3 $S/sync.py --list-only [--days-back N]` checks auth, refreshes the Fireflies DB, and prints `[{"id","title","date"}]` for transcripts not in the ledger. Its stderr line "N transcripts in last D days; M not yet exported" goes in the report. Exit 4 is auth: give the **Auth** message and stop. Exit 3: report stderr verbatim and stop. Other codes are in the script's docstring.
2. **Rename generic titles.** Check each pending title against `~/.claude/skills/name-meetings/REFERENCE.md` → Generic-title patterns. If any match, invoke `name-meetings` in **Unattended mode** (declare it), scoped to those ids: HIGH-confidence renames are applied, the rest go to `review[]` in the pending-renames file. Then re-run step 1.
3. **Export.** `python3 $S/sync.py --no-sync [--days-back N]` prints the new file paths. A meeting still generic after step 2 exports as it is and is named in the report.
4. **Add the header** to each step 3 path: prepend `~/.claude/skills/meeting-sync/assets/meeting-header.md` verbatim at the top. The Fireflies content below stays as it is. Notes from the 06:00 job already carry their own header.
5. **Tag the window.** Pass every note dated in the window, from both exporters, to the tagger (with `--days-back N`, use N for the 14):
   ```bash
   python3 -c "import glob,json,os,datetime as d; v=json.load(open(os.path.expanduser('~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.macos.json')))['vault_inbox_meetings']; cut=(d.date.today()-d.timedelta(days=14)).isoformat(); print('\n'.join(p for p in sorted(glob.glob(v+'/20*.md')) if os.path.basename(p)[:10]>=cut))" | xargs python3 $S/tag_project.py
   ```
   It skips notes that already hold a `<!-- jev-project:` marker or have no `## Project tags` header. For the rest it sends the Fireflies summary to TypeSafe's Jev (the flow Eric set up 2026-09-22), adds `- project/<PortfolioName>` when Jev is confident (≥ 0.60), and always writes one marker line. No key, no network or no transcript leaves a note untagged: relay each `WARNING` line.
6. **Report**, three lines: transcripts in the window, new exports and notes tagged; renames applied, queued for review, and any still-generic titles; the path `Inbox/meetings/`. With nothing new and nothing to tag: "No new meetings since last sync."

**Done when** every transcript in the window is in the ledger or named as a failed export, every note in the window has a `jev-project` marker or a relayed WARNING, and the report names every generic title left.

## Auth

Auth is the `FIREFLIES_API_KEY` environment variable. On exit 4, stop and tell the user:

> Fireflies isn't authenticated yet. On the Mac, store the key in the Keychain with `security add-generic-password -U -s FIREFLIES_API_KEY -a "$USER" -w` (it prompts for the key; `~/.zshrc` exports it). Then open a new terminal. After that, `/meeting-sync` will work.

The env var is the one mechanism: leave `auth set-token` alone.

Judge any wording change against meetings that test did not use.
